articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Data Dictionary Systems: Present and Future' (Digest No.55)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Data Dictionary Systems: Present and Future
IEE Colloquium on Data Dictionary Systems: Present and Future
abstract: Looks at the development of data dictionaries and at the work being undertaken by the International Standards Organisation, firmly supported by the British Standards Institution and the Department of Enterprise to develop standards for data dictionaries able to meet the needs and the challenges of the next ten years.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Data Dictionary Systems: Present and Future
abstract: The ICL data dictionary system (DDS) is used to hold information about an organisation and about the computer systems that serve it. This information is held in the form of elements and their properties.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The practical value of data dictionary systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Data Dictionary Systems: Present and Future
abstract: The DDS used by British Gas provides the information base from which the company develops systems to meet its own needs. Whilst individual project teams strive to achieve their users' requirements on schedule, the DDS provides the common framework to ensure that the separate pieces lock together in the overall business plan.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Data Dictionary Systems: Present and Future
abstract: Data modelling is the process of capturing in some understood representational format the 'details' needed to support the data and processing requirements of a database system application. Data models are traditionally thought of as comprising three parts: structures, operators and constants. Current trends in this field are examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
